wordpress_analytics.desc: WordPress Analytics settings. For the most recent version of the plugin, please visit the plugin's Github page. For support, feel free to open an issue on Github.

measurement_id.title: Google Analytics 4 measurement ID
measurement_id.desc: To what Google Analytics 4 property should the data be sent to? The ID is in the form G-XXXXXXXXXX. You can find it in the GA admin, under Data streams, in the details of the web stream.

load_mode.title: Who loads Google Analytics 4?
load_mode.desc: Choose 'WordPress Analytics' if nothing else loads GA4 on this website: the plugin will print the Google tag and pageviews will be sent. Choose 'Google Tag Manager' if GA4 is already loaded by GTM or by another plugin: WordPress Analytics will not print the Google tag, so that pageviews are not counted twice. Choose 'Nobody' to use only the custom code and the phone number features.

options.gtm: Google Tag Manager or another plugin

scroll_tracking.title: Enable scroll tracking?
scroll_tracking.desc: Send events to Google Analytics based on the user scrolling activity on each page.

call_tracking.title: Enable call tracking?
call_tracking.desc: Send an event to Google Analytics every time a user clicks on a phone number.

form_tracking.title: Enable form tracking?
form_tracking.desc: Send an event to Google Analytics every time a user submits a form; for now the feature works only for forms made with the Gravity Forms plugin. The event has the action field seet to 'form:' followed by the form title. The event label is the path of the post which contains the form. If the form is a payment form, the event label will also include the transaction ID and transaction amount. The events are sent using the measurement protocol with anonymized IPs; this means that the IP associated to the hit will be, for example, 77.123.456.000 instead of 77.123.456.789, and that ad blockers won't block the event.'

email_tracking.title: Enable email tracking?
email_tracking.desc: Send an event to Google Analytics every time a user clicks on an email address.

content_grouping.title: Enable content grouping?
content_grouping.desc: Send the WordPress category of each post (or 'Prodotti' for WooCommerce products) to Google Analytics 4 as the content group of the page. Works only when the Google tag is loaded by WordPress Analytics.

scroll_tracking.desc:
Settings for the scroll tracking functionality.

Parameters set here will be ignored if you have Javascript caching enabled.

pixel_threshold.title: Pixels threshold for engagement
pixel_threshold.desc: Pixels the user needs to scroll before we consider him/her engaged.

time_threshold.title: Seconds required to read content
time_threshold.desc: Time in seconds the user needs to spend on the content before we consider it read

call_tracking.desc:
Settings for the call tracking functionality.

Parameters set here will be ignored if you have Javascript caching enabled.

phone_regex_include_pattern.title: Phone pattern (include)
phone_regex_include_pattern.desc: Consider only phone numbers that match this pattern; leave blank to catch all clicks to 'tel:' links.

phone_regex_exclude_pattern.title: Phone pattern (exclude)
phone_regex_exclude_pattern.desc: Do not consider phone numbers that match this regex pattern; leave blank to catch all clicks to 'tel:' links.

detect_phone_numbers.title: Detect phone numbers automatically
detect_phone_numbers.desc: If set, automatically convert the pattern 'TEL: +39 06 123456' into a phone number link. Useful if you can't input HTML in pages, ex. in a Visual Composer module.

wait_for_form_payment.title: Wait for payment confirmation
wait_for_form_payment.desc: When enabled, the form submission event will be sent to GA only after a successful payment. If you disable this option, the event will be sent immediately after form submission, without waiting for payment confirmation.

enable_json_folder.title: Look for JSON meta boxes
enable_json_folder.desc: Include the meta boxes found in the 'acf' subfolder of the plugin folder; these must be in the ACF JSON Format.

network_mode.title: Network Mode
network_mode.desc: Manage plugin options only at the network level, preventing site admins to change them. IMPORTANT:: Until I find a way to use the Settings API to set options in the network admin (ex. using http://wordpress.stackexchange.com/a/72503/86662), the plugin options will be set and read from the main blog admin page rather than the network admin page.

send_page_view.title: Send pageview to GA?
send_page_view.desc: Should the Google tag printed by WordPress Analytics send a pageview to Google Analytics 4 when the page loads? Turn it off if the pageview is sent by something else, ex. by your own code. It has no effect if Google Analytics 4 is not loaded by WordPress Analytics.

debug.title: Debug mode
debug.desc: Log the plugin's activity to file. Two files will be written: debug.log in the plugin's folder and debug.log in the wp-content folder. Furthermore, javascript-related activity will be shown in the browser's console.

debug_email.title: Debug email
debug_email.desc: This email address will be notified whenever the plugin generates a serious error; leave empty to disable the feature. Please note that the email will be sent regardless of the value of the 'debug' flag.

custom_code.title: Custom code
custom_code.desc: Any code you write here will be included in the head of all pages of your website, whether Google Analytics is configured or not. Remember to include the PHP opening & closing tags.

attributes.placeholder: Code written here will be injected in the head of the document. Remember the <?php tag to write PHP code.
